summary: Gavin Flood is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Lancaster University (~1983–1988) under Andrew Rawlinson and David Smith. He held posts at Lampeter (~1991–1998), Stirling (~1998–2005), and Oxford and the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies (~2005).

Gelek is a Tibetologist who has served as a researcher at the China Tibetology Research Center, a visiting lecturer at the University of California, and a visiting scholar at the University of Oxford.

Gembo Dorji is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Tango Buddhist College, the East-West Center, and the University of Tokyo. He trained under Tenzin Dhendrup, Dongyud Nyima, Jigme Choedra, Kuenlay Gyeltshen, Sonam Jamtsho, Sangay Dorji, and Sendrak Rinpoche.
Gen'ichi Yamazaki was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1954–1965) and served as a professor at Kokugakuin University in 1999.
Genchi Kato was a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1896 to 1899 and later held a post there from ~1919 to 1934.

Gendun Chophel was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kumbum Monastery (~1917–1920), Labrang Monastery (1920), and under Sherab Gyatso (~1920–1927). He held a post at the Maha Bodhi Society in 1941.

Genjun Sasaki was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Kyoto University and under several mentors, including P. V. Bapat and V. V. Gokhale. He held posts at Otani, Osaka, Hamburg, and Harvard.
Genryu Kagamishima was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from ~1930 to 1934 and later served there as a professor from ~1954 to 1983.
Gensho Imanari was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied at Waseda University (~1948–1955). He held posts at Kokushikan University (~1968–1974) and Rissho University (~1974–1996).

Gensho Takenuki was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Otani University (~1964–1968) and Bukkyo University (~1971–1976), and held posts at Shogen Junior College and Hanazono University (~1987–2016).
Genzao was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Dzogchen Monastery until 1950, and trained under Gyang mdzod Rinpoche (1948) and Kalu Rinpoche.

Geo Widengren was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. He studied at Stockholm University (~1925–1927) and Uppsala University (~1927–1936), later holding posts at Stockholm University and Uppsala University (~1940–1973).

Geoff Childs is a Tibetology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Indiana University (~1993–1998) under Tsetan Chonjore. He held posts at the Australian National University (~1999–2001) and Washington University in St. Louis (~2001–2007).
Geoffrey Barstow is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He held posts at the University of Virginia (~2006–2013) and Oregon State University (~2015).
Geoffrey Cantor is a scholar of history/archaeology, religious studies, and philosophy who held posts at Indiana University (~1969–1970) and the University of Leeds (1973).

Geoffrey Goble is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He studied at the University of Virginia (~2004–2006) and Indiana University (~2006–2012), later becoming assistant professor of religious studies at the University of Oklahoma (~2016).

Geoffrey Samuel is a scholar of religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Cambridge under Edmund Leach, Stanley Tambiah, and Peter Wilson, and held posts at Newcastle (~1975–2004), Lancaster (~1995–1999), and Cardiff (~2005–2014).

Georg Buddruss was an Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. He studied at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1948–1954) and the University of Tübingen, and served as professor at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1963–1995).

Georg Bühler was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen (1855–1858) under Theodor Benfey and Hermann Sauppe. He held posts at Elphinstone College, the University of Mumbai (~1863–1880), and the University of Vienna (1880–1898).

Georg Curtius was a linguist who studied at Bonn under Ritschl and Lassen (~1837–1838) and Berlin under Bopp (~1838–1840). He held posts at Charles University (~1849–1854), University of Kiel (~1854–1862), and Leipzig University (~1862–1885).
